issues.description: Fix `range`/`text` in reject test cases look wrong and inconsistent with the `fixed` output
issues.detail: Several reject cases set `fix.text: '0deg'` while the `fixed` string shows the inserted text as `10deg` or `120deg`. The range/text pair should describe the actual edit applied. If the test harness ignores `fix` when `fixed` is present this is dead noise; if it validates, these tests are wrong. Either way the diff ships confusion.

`args[0 + offset]` is the kind of cleverness that adds noise without meaning. Write `args[offset]` and `args[2 + offset]` stays as is, or define a single index. Small thing, but it is exactly the kind of style nit the next maintainer notices.

issues.description: Optional-chain on `args[0]?.value` masks a real invariant
issues.detail: `args` is filtered to word/function nodes — if it is empty the function call had no channels and the rule has nothing to check. The `?.` is defensive against a case that cannot meaningfully reach here. Not wrong, just imprecise about what the code actually expects.

issues.description: Nested relative color `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` only covered in accept path
issues.detail: The accept test covers the nested case, but there is no reject test that exercises a nested relative color where the inner function contains a violating hue. The fix walks `args` only at the outer level; inner function nodes are handled by recursion elsewhere, but a reject test would lock that behavior in.

issues.description: Case-sensitivity of `from` is tested once; behavior for mixed-case function name unverified
issues.detail: Test uses `FROM` to confirm the lowercase comparison. Good. But the function `value` is also lowercased via `node.value.toLowerCase()` — no test covers `OKLCH(from ...)` style. Cheap to add, would prevent future regression if someone removes the lowercase call.

review.summary: Small, focused patch. Solves a real bug (relative color syntax shifts the hue channel by two) with a four-line change and a credible set of accept/reject tests. Good taste: no special-casing per function, just an offset applied uniformly. Bad taste: `args[0 + offset]` instead of `args[offset]`, and the `fix.text` fields in several new reject cases disagree with the `fixed` strings, which is either a test-harness footgun or a real bug in the fixtures. NEEDS-WORK: clean up the test fixtures, drop the `0 +`, and this lands.
